newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Aid teams find starving children in west Liberia.
newsitem.headline: Aid teams find starving children in west Liberia.

text.p: Relief workers found severely malnourished children in Liberia's southwestern Cape Mount region on Wednesday, after being denied access to the area for six months by factional fighting, a spokesman said.

An assessment team, similar to one that discovered hundreds of starving children and old people in the town of Tubmanburg earlier this month, discovered malnourished people in five towns and related villages in the area, Kent Page of the U.N. said.
But reports of fresh fighting on Wednesday prevented the team reaching their intended destination of Bo-Waterside on the Sierra Leone border, he added.

"It is believed that more and more malnourished children and sick persons will appear from the forests in the next few days as word spreads that the humanitarian community has finally been allowed back," Page said.
Page said Cape Mount deaths rates were difficult to confirm but a local group had spoken of 403 hunger related deaths since April. One child died of hunger at Mani village on Wednesday.

The two factions vying for control of the area -- erstwhile allies in the Mandingo ULIMO-K and Krahn ULIMO-J factions -- signed an agreement on Tuesday granting the relief groups unconditional safe passage into the area.
West African peacekeepers ventured into Cape Mount for the first time since January on Monday, after militia gunmen blocked three attempts by relief groups to reach the area.
Relief agencies believe that pockets of hungry Liberians may exist elsewhere in the country.
Displaced people near the southern port of Buchanan say civilians are dying from lack of food and medicine after fleeing clashes between two other rival factions in the southeast.
All the factions fought in the capital Monrovia in April and May. Hundreds of people died in clashes.
More than 150,000 people have died since 1989 in the civil war in Liberia, founded by freed American slaves in 1847.

West African leaders rallied faction leaders round a new peace deal in August and backed it with the threat of sanctions against anyone derailing the agreement. It evisages disarmament by January of next year and elections by May.
